title: Nine hikers fled their tent into the snow

lines.text: In 1959, nine experienced hikers cut their way out of their own tent and ran into the snow.
It happened on a slope in Russia's northern Ural Mountains.
Investigators found the tent slashed open from the inside.
Many were barely dressed, some in socks or one shoe, at around minus thirty degrees.
Six died of hypothermia. Three had severe injuries, like skull and chest fractures.
For decades, people blamed everything from secret weapons to aliens.
In 2020, Russian prosecutors officially blamed an avalanche.
And in 2021, scientists simulated how a small slab of snow could crush a tent and cause injuries like these.
But many still don't believe it. Why would nine experts run into the dark without their boots?

sources.claim: 1 or 2 February 1959, nine hikers died in the northern Urals; tent cut open from inside; many partly dressed; about −25 to −30 °C
Six died of hypothermia, three of fatal trauma (skull and chest injuries)
2020 prosecutor ruling: avalanche; 2021 Gaume and Puzrin slab-avalanche simulation
